$comment: Generalized from ccar-p data/recap-rules.json (recap_rule -> syllabus_rule). The 24 architectural rules behind the weak-rule report.

rules.title: Decomposition is the move that comes before architecture
rules.gloss: Split the work into what Claude handles, what existing systems handle, and what humans handle — before choosing any pattern.

rules.title: Choosing a pattern is choosing how much autonomy to grant
rules.gloss: Augmented LLM, workflow and agent sit on an autonomy spectrum; five factors decide, and the tightest constraint is the one that picks.

rules.title: Reach for the tested reference architectures before inventing your own
rules.gloss: Five documented architectures exist because teams already learned what breaks in each. Never use retrieval as a substitute for live state.

rules.title: Choosing a model: start with Sonnet and treat every swap as a release
rules.gloss: Sonnet is the default tier. Any swap needs an eval set defining better and a rollback criterion fixed beforehand. Progressive context outlasts monolithic context.

rules.title: Pick the entry point by the work it has to do, not by what is already on the shelf
rules.gloss: Claude.ai, the API, the SDK, Claude Code and MCP each trade something different. Name the trade-off when you recommend one.

rules.title: Evals as acceptance criteria
rules.gloss: Write the eval suite before the production code, keep the golden dataset current, and gate every model swap or prompt revision on it.

rules.title: POC to production
rules.gloss: Estimate cost and latency at production volume, build retries, fallback chains and circuit breakers in from the start, and name your architecture's failure mode with its mitigation.

rules.title: Use-case sizing and feasibility
rules.gloss: Run each use case through the four AI properties, then state a verdict: feasible as scoped, feasible with constraints, or not feasible — documenting the load-bearing boundary condition.

rules.title: Enterprise integration patterns
rules.gloss: Enforce identity server-side, pass only the minimum necessary data into context, and instrument observability at design time.

rules.title: A/B testing and observability
rules.gloss: Fix the primary metric and sample size before running anything, separate per-request traces from aggregate dashboards, and translate technical metrics into business ones.

rules.title: Safety is a stack of layers, not a setting
rules.gloss: Training never saw your domain policy, data rules or authorization model. The dangerous failure is silent: assuming a rule is enforced when it lives in no layer.

rules.title: A guarded path has three control points and a chosen failure direction
rules.gloss: Input screening, output screening and tool-call authorization answer different questions, so one filter at the end covers none of the others. Fail closed where a wrong pass causes harm.

rules.title: Fairness and transparency are instrumented, not assumed
rules.gloss: Unequal outcomes arise at points you control — corpus, prompt framing, examples, routing. Log every decision, because an explanation you cannot reconstruct you cannot give.

rules.title: Route review by stakes, not by volume
rules.gloss: Confidence, reversibility and the cost of a wrong answer decide what a human sees. Route everything and the queue floods until reviewers stop reading.

rules.title: A compliant entry point is a prerequisite, and an evidenced control set is the proof
rules.gloss: Turn each obligation into a specific control, a named owner and a living evidence artifact. A control with neither goes non-operational and fails the audit.

rules.title: Structured discovery
rules.gloss: Run discovery as a four-category process, translate every preference into a constraint, and write requirement rows with their assumptions labelled.

rules.title: Communicating tradeoffs
rules.gloss: Present every trade-off in three elements, including the reversal cost, and let the accountable stakeholder decide informed.

rules.title: Feedback loops and SLA management
rules.gloss: Build the decision layer mapping signals to trigger actions to owners, set SLA thresholds from their real sources, and schedule regulated checkpoints.

rules.title: Documentation for handoff and audit
rules.gloss: Record the decision, the rejected alternatives and the trade-off each resolved while you still hold the reasoning, and carry the control register forward.

rules.title: Entry point selection and outcomes
rules.gloss: Choose the route on latency, compliance and cost, map responsibility across multi-entry-point designs, and capture the before metric, the auditable control and the reuse note.

rules.title: Team setup is shared configuration, distribution, and spend posture decided up front
rules.gloss: A shared baseline plus a Skills distribution approach — org-provisioned, plugins, project Skills, API Skills — all bounded by model and budget guardrails.

rules.title: Adoption is engineered through champions and batches
rules.gloss: A champion per team proves the workflow and seeds adoption. Access without enablement stalls at basic chat; lumpy adoption never standardises the gain.

rules.title: Diligence keeps AI-assisted work trustworthy
rules.gloss: Hold AI-generated code to correctness, security and maintainability, require the author to explain what shipped, and gate on a verification checklist.

rules.title: Operational support is translation plus self-sufficiency
rules.gloss: Connect symptoms to architecture causes, and leave runbooks and escalation paths so the team needs you for the new problem, not the familiar one.
